find_species.description: Find species in NOAA Fisheries' species list by common or Latin name, with the number FOSS files each under, the name as its data writes it, its family, whether it is finfish or shellfish, its habitat, whether it is protected and whether FOSS reports landings for it. Use it to find the exact species before reading landings.

find_trade_products.description: Find the traded products whose names contain a word, such as every salmon product, with their 10-digit tariff codes, NOAA's product group, whether they are food, and what was traded in one year, largest first. Trade is counted by product rather than species, so this is how to find the right name or code to pass to the other trade actions.

get_landings.description: Read what US fishermen landed, year by year: the pounds brought to the dock and what they sold for, for one species or every species together, in one state, one region or the whole country. Choose recreational to get what anglers kept instead, as weight and number of fish. Defaults to the last ten years NOAA has published, and says how much the value changed and which year was the peak. Figures withheld for confidentiality are counted and never taken for zeros.

description: Read the United States' official fishery statistics from NOAA Fisheries' One Stop Shop: what commercial fishermen landed in each state since 1950 and what it sold for, what recreational anglers kept since 1980, seafood imports and exports by product and country every month, what US processors produced, the Alaska bottom trawl surveys station by station, and the Coast Guard's register of documented vessels. Rank the species landed in a state or the partners the US buys shrimp from, follow a species' landings over ten years, or read the Bering Sea's bottom temperature. No account or API key required.
